title: Choose Workroom's visual world
question: Keep the press-proof direction, choose an alternate, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: Patch Proofing Table
options.lineage: industrial print proofing tables and imposition sheets
options.thesis: Every task is a separate galley, aligned into one inspectable working sheet.
options.viewport: A huge working proof sheet pairs the download promise with a live-looking arrangement of parallel workrooms, diff marks, and registration controls.
options.risk: Can feel like print nostalgia if the grid is decorative instead of visibly organizing real product proof.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: Workroom becomes a direct-address developer broadcast with every feature on a numbered page.
options.viewport: A rigid bitmap screen indexes WORKROOM 100, SPLITS 210, DIFFS 302, and DOWNLOAD 900 around a product capture.
options.risk: Strong developer recognition, but page-by-page navigation fights Workroom's promise of simultaneous split contexts.
options.case: Loses narrowly on product clarity: culturally legible, structurally too sequential.

options.label: Glazier's Partition
options.thesis: Parallel work becomes a wall of clear panes, each context lit independently but visible together.
options.viewport: A full-height glazing elevation makes the app screenshot and download action the two illuminated panes in a larger workroom wall.
options.risk: The split-view mechanism reads instantly, but the material has weaker native vocabulary for code review, diffs, and VCS state.
options.case: Nearly ties on clarity; loses on developer identification and VCS specificity.

options.label: Cut-Paper Sequence
options.thesis: Workroom's mechanism unfolds through hard, cinematic cards of isolated tasks converging into one release.
options.viewport: A black worktree shape fractures across a yellow field while one decisive line lands on Download the beta.
options.risk: The timed sequence hides the simultaneous, inspectable contexts the homepage must prove immediately.
options.case: Fuses poorly because cinematic sequence contradicts Workroom's parallel visibility.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A restrained dark product page with a large app screenshot, feature rows, and an unmistakable beta download.
canonCard.viewport: A centered headline and download button sit above the annotated Workroom screenshot with concise proof below.
canonCard.risk: Clear and credible, but unlikely to make Workroom memorable beyond its category.
